verses.he: בָּ֣אתִי לְגַנִּי֮ אֲחֹתִ֣י כַלָּה֒ אָרִ֤יתִי מוֹרִי֙ עִם־בְּשָׂמִ֔י אָכַ֤לְתִּי יַעְרִי֙ עִם־דִּבְשִׁ֔י שָׁתִ֥יתִי יֵינִ֖י עִם־חֲלָבִ֑י אִכְל֣וּ רֵעִ֔ים שְׁת֥וּ וְשִׁכְר֖וּ דּוֹדִֽים׃
verses.en: I have come to my garden, my sister, my bride; I have gathered my myrrh with my spice. I have eaten my honeycomb with my honey; I have drunk my wine with my milk. Eat, friends; drink, yes, drink deeply, beloved ones.
verses.tr: bā֣ʾtiy ləganiy֮ ʾăḥōti֣y kalāh֒ ʾāri֤ytiy mwōriy֙ ʿim-bəšāmi֔y ʾāka֤lətiy yaʿəriy֙ ʿim-dibəši֔y šāti֥ytiy yēyni֖y ʿim-ḥălābi֑y ʾikəl֣w rēʿi֔ym šət֥w wəšikər֖w dwōdiym.

verses.he: אֲנִ֥י יְשֵׁנָ֖ה וְלִבִּ֣י עֵ֑ר ק֣וֹל ׀ דּוֹדִ֣י דוֹפֵ֗ק פִּתְחִי־לִ֞י אֲחֹתִ֤י רַעְיָתִי֙ יוֹנָתִ֣י תַמָּתִ֔י שֶׁרֹּאשִׁי֙ נִמְלָא־טָ֔ל קְוֻּצּוֹתַ֖י רְסִ֥יסֵי לָֽיְלָה׃
verses.en: I was sleeping, but my heart was awake. A sound—my beloved is knocking: “Open to me, my sister, my love, my dove, my perfect one; for my head is filled with dew, my locks with the drops of the night.”
verses.tr: ʾăni֥y yəšēnā֖h wəlibi֣y ʿē֑r q֣wōl | dwōdi֣y dwōpē֗q pitəḥiy-li֞y ʾăḥōti֤y raʿəyātiy֙ ywōnāti֣y tamāti֔y šerōʾšiy֙ niməlāʾ-ṭā֔l qəwuṣwōta֖y rəsi֥ysēy lāyəlāh.

verses.he: פָּשַׁ֨טְתִּי֙ אֶת־כֻּתָּנְתִּ֔י אֵיכָ֖כָה אֶלְבָּשֶׁ֑נָּה רָחַ֥צְתִּי אֶת־רַגְלַ֖י אֵיכָ֥כָה אֲטַנְּפֵֽם׃
verses.en: I have taken off my tunic—how can I put it on? I have washed my feet—how can I soil them?
verses.tr: pāša֨ṭətiy֙ ʾet-kutānəti֔y ʾēykā֖kāh ʾeləbāše֑nāh rāḥa֥ṣətiy ʾet-ragəla֖y ʾēykā֥kāh ʾăṭanəpēm.

verses.he: דּוֹדִ֗י שָׁלַ֤ח יָדוֹ֙ מִן־הַחֹ֔ר וּמֵעַ֖י הָמ֥וּ עָלָֽיו׃
verses.en: My beloved put his hand through the opening, and my inward parts yearned for him.
verses.tr: dwōdi֗y šāla֤ḥ yādwō֙ min-haḥō֔r wmēʿa֖y hām֥w ʿālāyw.

verses.he: קַ֥מְתִּֽי אֲנִ֖י לִפְתֹּ֣חַ לְדוֹדִ֑י וְיָדַ֣י נָֽטְפוּ־מ֗וֹר וְאֶצְבְּעֹתַי֙ מ֣וֹר עֹבֵ֔ר עַ֖ל כַּפּ֥וֹת הַמַּנְעֽוּל׃
verses.en: I rose to open to my beloved, and my hands dripped with myrrh, my fingers with flowing myrrh on the handles of the bolt.
verses.tr: qa֥mətiy ʾăni֖y lipətō֣ḥa lədwōdi֑y wəyāda֣y nāṭəpw-m֗wōr wəʾeṣəbəʿōtay֙ m֣wōr ʿōbē֔r ʿa֖l kap֥wōt hamanəʿwl.

verses.he: פָּתַ֤חְתִּֽי אֲנִי֙ לְדוֹדִ֔י וְדוֹדִ֖י חָמַ֣ק עָבָ֑ר נַפְשִׁי֙ יָֽצְאָ֣ה בְדַבְּר֔וֹ בִּקַּשְׁתִּ֨יהוּ֙ וְלֹ֣א מְצָאתִ֔יהוּ קְרָאתִ֖יו וְלֹ֥א עָנָֽנִי׃
verses.en: I opened to my beloved, but my beloved had turned and gone. My soul went out at his speaking; I sought him but did not find him. I called him, but he did not answer me.
verses.tr: pāta֤ḥətiy ʾăniy֙ lədwōdi֔y wədwōdi֖y ḥāma֣q ʿābā֑r napəšiy֙ yāṣəʾā֣h bədabər֔wō biqašəti֨yhw֙ wəlō֣ʾ məṣāʾti֔yhw qərāʾti֖yw wəlō֥ʾ ʿānāniy.

verses.he: מְצָאֻ֧נִי הַשֹּׁמְרִ֛ים הַסֹּבְבִ֥ים בָּעִ֖יר הִכּ֣וּנִי פְצָע֑וּנִי נָשְׂא֤וּ אֶת־רְדִידִי֙ מֵֽעָלַ֔י שֹׁמְרֵ֖י הַחֹמֽוֹת׃
verses.en: The watchmen who go about the city found me; they struck me, they wounded me; they took away my veil from me—the watchmen of the walls.
verses.tr: məṣāʾu֧niy hašōməri֛ym hasōbəbi֥ym bāʿi֖yr hik֣wniy pəṣāʿ֑wniy nāšəʾ֤w ʾet-rədiydiy֙ mēʿāla֔y šōmərē֖y haḥōmwōt.

verses.he: הִשְׁבַּ֥עְתִּי אֶתְכֶ֖ם בְּנ֣וֹת יְרוּשָׁלִָ֑ם אִֽם־תִּמְצְאוּ֙ אֶת־דּוֹדִ֔י מַה־תַּגִּ֣ידוּ ל֔וֹ שֶׁחוֹלַ֥ת אַהֲבָ֖ה אָֽנִי׃
verses.en: I adjure you, daughters of Jerusalem: if you find my beloved, what will you tell him?—that I am sick with love.
verses.tr: hišəba֥ʿətiy ʾetəke֖m bən֣wōt yərwšālā֑im ʾim-timəṣəʾw֙ ʾet-dwōdi֔y mah-tagi֣ydw l֔wō šeḥwōla֥t ʾahăbā֖h ʾāniy.

verses.he: מַה־דּוֹדֵ֣ךְ מִדּ֔וֹד הַיָּפָ֖ה בַּנָּשִׁ֑ים מַה־דּוֹדֵ֣ךְ מִדּ֔וֹד שֶׁכָּ֖כָה הִשְׁבַּעְתָּֽנוּ׃
verses.en: What is your beloved more than another beloved, O fairest among women? What is your beloved more than another beloved, that you adjure us so?
verses.tr: mah-dwōdē֣kə mid֔wōd hayāpā֖h banāši֑ym mah-dwōdē֣kə mid֔wōd šekā֖kāh hišəbaʿətānw.

verses.en: My beloved is radiant and ruddy, distinguished among ten thousand.

verses.he: רֹאשׁ֖וֹ כֶּ֣תֶם פָּ֑ז קְוּצּוֹתָיו֙ תַּלְתַּלִּ֔ים שְׁחֹר֖וֹת כָּעוֹרֵֽב׃
verses.en: His head is finest gold; his locks are wavy, black as a raven.
verses.tr: rōʾš֖wō ke֣tem pā֑z qəwṣwōtāyw֙ talətali֔ym šəḥōr֖wōt kāʿwōrēb.

verses.he: עֵינָ֕יו כְּיוֹנִ֖ים עַל־אֲפִ֣יקֵי מָ֑יִם רֹֽחֲצוֹת֙ בֶּֽחָלָ֔ב יֹשְׁב֖וֹת עַל־מִלֵּֽאת׃
verses.en: His eyes are like doves by streams of water, washed with milk, sitting in fullness.
verses.tr: ʿēynā֕yw kəywōni֖ym ʿal-ʾăpi֣yqēy mā֑yim rōḥăṣwōt֙ beḥālā֔b yōšəb֖wōt ʿal-milēʾt.

verses.he: לְחָיָו֙ כַּעֲרוּגַ֣ת הַבֹּ֔שֶׂם מִגְדְּל֖וֹת מֶרְקָחִ֑ים שִׂפְתוֹתָיו֙ שֽׁוֹשַׁנִּ֔ים נֹטְפ֖וֹת מ֥וֹר עֹבֵֽר׃
verses.en: His cheeks are like beds of spice, towers of perfumes; his lips are lilies, dripping flowing myrrh.
verses.tr: ləḥāyāw֙ kaʿărwga֣t habō֔šem migədəl֖wōt merəqāḥi֑ym šipətwōtāyw֙ šwōšani֔ym nōṭəp֖wōt m֥wōr ʿōbēr.

verses.he: יָדָיו֙ גְּלִילֵ֣י זָהָ֔ב מְמֻלָּאִ֖ים בַּתַּרְשִׁ֑ישׁ מֵעָיו֙ עֶ֣שֶׁת שֵׁ֔ן מְעֻלֶּ֖פֶת סַפִּירִֽים׃
verses.en: His hands are rods of gold set with beryl; his body is ivory work overlaid with sapphires.
verses.tr: yādāyw֙ gəliylē֣y zāhā֔b məmulāʾi֖ym batarəši֑yš mēʿāyw֙ ʿe֣šet šē֔n məʿule֖pet sapiyriym.

verses.he: שׁוֹקָיו֙ עַמּ֣וּדֵי שֵׁ֔שׁ מְיֻסָּדִ֖ים עַל־אַדְנֵי־פָ֑ז מַרְאֵ֨הוּ֙ כַּלְּבָנ֔וֹן בָּח֖וּר כָּאֲרָזִֽים׃
verses.en: His legs are pillars of marble set on bases of fine gold; his appearance is like Lebanon, choice as the cedars.
verses.tr: šwōqāyw֙ ʿam֣wdēy šē֔š məyusādi֖ym ʿal-ʾadənēy-pā֑z marəʾē֨hw֙ kaləbān֔wōn bāḥ֖wr kāʾărāziym.

verses.he: חִכּוֹ֙ מַֽמְתַקִּ֔ים וְכֻלּ֖וֹ מַחֲּמַדִּ֑ים זֶ֤ה דוֹדִי֙ וְזֶ֣ה רֵעִ֔י בְּנ֖וֹת יְרוּשָׁלִָֽם׃
verses.en: His mouth is sweetness, and he is altogether desirable. This is my beloved and this is my friend, O daughters of Jerusalem.
verses.tr: ḥikwō֙ mamətaqi֔ym wəkul֖wō maḥămadi֑ym ze֤h dwōdiy֙ wəze֣h rēʿi֔y bən֖wōt yərwšālāim.

grammar.title: 1cs perfect narrative chain
grammar.body:
A sequence of 1cs perfect verbs forms a stylized recounting of completed actions.

Example: בָּאתִי … אָרִיתִי … אָכַלְתִּי … שָׁתִיתִי (5:1)

grammar.title: Imperatives + vocatives
grammar.body:
Direct address stacks vocatives; imperative 2fs (‘open!’) drives the scene.

Example: פִּתְחִי־לִי … אֲחֹתִי רַעְיָתִי … (5:2)

grammar.title: Rhetorical ‘how?’ question
grammar.body:
אֵיכָכָה introduces rhetorical reluctance (‘how could I…?’).

Example: אֵיכָכָה אֶלְבָּשֶׁנָּה … אֵיכָכָה אֲטַנְּפֵם (5:3)

grammar.title: Pronominal suffixes
grammar.body:
Suffixes mark possession and participant tracking; they are pervasive in description.

Example: דוֹדִי / לִבִּי / נַפְשִׁי / יָדַי / אֶצְבְּעֹתַי

grammar.title: Object marker אֶת
grammar.body:
אֶת marks definite direct objects; it is usually not translated.

Example: אֶת־כֻּתָּנְתִּי; אֶת־רַגְלַי; אֶת־רְדִידִי

grammar.title: Participles as depiction
grammar.body:
Participles function adjectivally to depict ongoing action/qualities in the portrait.

Example: דוֹפֵק; רֹחֲצוֹת; יֹשְׁבוֹת; נֹטְפוֹת

exercises.q: In 5:1, list the four 1cs perfect verbs and translate them.
exercises.a: בָּאתִי ‘I came’; אָרִיתִי ‘I gathered’; אָכַלְתִּי ‘I ate’; שָׁתִיתִי ‘I drank’.

exercises.q: Identify the imperative in 5:2 and its addressee.
exercises.a: פִּתְחִי־לִי ‘Open to me!’ addressed to the woman (2fs).

exercises.q: What discourse effect does אֵיכָכָה have in 5:3?
exercises.a: It frames reluctance as a rhetorical question (‘how could I…?’).

exercises.q: Name two verbs reused from 3:1–2 in 5:6 and give their meaning.
exercises.a: בִּקַּשְׁתִּיהוּ ‘I sought him’; מְצָאתִיהוּ ‘I found him’ (negated here: ‘did not find’).
PLACE (city/walls), DAMAGE (struck/wounded), PERCEPTION (encounter), LOVE (context of search).
A praise-portrait (wasf) describes the beloved from head to legs using precious-material and nature imagery.
